observations: Photo 0 shows a close-up of a gas valve with '07 07' stamped on the side.
Photo 1 shows a tall, white, vertical cylinder with a protective collar at the top.
The white cylinder in Photo 1 has visible surface rust on the weld seams and scratches on the body.
Photo 2 shows two cylinders: one tall black cylinder with a white neck/shoulder and one white cylinder.
The black and white cylinder is taller than the white cylinder and lacks a protective collar.
The color coding (black body, white top) is consistent with industrial oxygen cylinders.
The white cylinder is a standard design for LPG (cooking gas).
Stamping is visible on the collar of the white cylinder in Photo 1 but is too blurry to read.

claims.evidence: Photo 2 shows an oxygen cylinder and a large LPG cylinder, both used in industrial/commercial settings.
The capacity stamps on the shoulder of the black cylinder are not shown in any photo.
The stamps on the collar in Photo 1 are illegible.

risks.risk: Cylinders may be expired or past their mandatory re-test date.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped manufacture or test date on the collar (white) or shoulder (black).

risks.risk: Actual capacity may be smaller than the seller's claim.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped Water Capacity (WC) or Tare Weight (TW) on the cylinder.
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest standard size (e.g., 12.5kg for the LPG cylinder)

risks.risk: Valves may be seized, leaking, or have damaged threads.
risks.proof: A video showing the valves being operated and a soap-bubble leak test if pressurized.

proof_requests: Clear, legible photos of the stamped markings on the collar of the white LPG cylinder.
Clear, legible photos of the stamped markings on the shoulder of the black oxygen cylinder.
A video showing both valves being opened and closed.
response.reason: The capacity and expiry dates, which are the primary drivers of value and safety for gas cylinders, are stamped into the metal but are not legible in the provided photos.
